The Dutch-taught Public Administration degree studies how policy, government and public organisations shape societal problems, and how their effects can be understood and improved. It combines political, legal, economic and social perspectives with empirical research.

Three UCR routes offer related study in public policy and institutions, climate governance, or public organisations and digital change. Radboud adds a dedicated public-administration sequence, Dutch policy practice and a separate bachelor thesis. The UCR routes develop related academic capacities and do not confer the same disciplinary qualification.

Academic year: 2026–2027

External pathway: General programme; two restricted electives

The displayed restricted electives are one possible pair from four options and are subject to available places. Course offerings and applicable regulations may change.

What this comparison shows

A curriculum-level comparison of Public Administration at Radboud University with 3 illustrative UCR study compositions.

CLOSEST UCR MATCH
Public policy, governance & institutions

A broad route through public policy and governance, combining political and legal institutions, public economics, sociology, civil society, organisational psychology, European governance and quantitative and qualitative inquiry. Dedicated policy implementation, Dutch administration and a separate public-administration thesis remain specialist gaps.

ADDITIONAL UCR OPTION
Climate policy & sustainability governance

A climate-policy and sustainability-governance route centred on public institutions, law, public economics, participation, environmental justice, communication and empirical methods. Climate science, planetary boundaries and life-cycle assessment provide specific grounding for policy choices; regional sustainability research supplies applied practice without guaranteeing a policy topic.

ADDITIONAL UCR OPTION
Public organisations, leadership & digital governance

A route centred on public organisations, leadership and digital governance. Comparative politics, public international law, constitutional law, EU politics and civil society anchor organisational psychology, communication, quantitative and qualitative methods. AI governance and social-venture creation supply specific complementary tools for organisational change.

Important limitation

This is a curriculum comparison. A UCR composition is not the same disciplinary degree and does not by itself establish a professional qualification or automatic eligibility for a particular master’s programme.

Rows show curricular relationships, including partial matches, rather than course equivalence. A blank cell means there is no closely comparable component in that row. Optional independent research is additional to the displayed 180 EC.
